dedupe_keys.name: umep urban multi scale environmental predictor qgis plugin for urban climate modelling

description: UMEP is an open-source climate service tool delivered as a QGIS plugin for researchers and practitioners such as architects, climatologists and energy, health and urban planners, used for outdoor thermal comfort, urban energy consumption and climate change mitigation. It couples 1D and 2D urban climate models with scale-independent coverage from street to city, with pre-processors that derive model parameters from spatial data in QGIS, processors and post-processors. The processors include ExtremeFinder and SOLWEIG for outdoor thermal comfort, daily shadow patterns and SEBE for solar energy on building envelopes, GQ, LQ and SUEWS (simple and advanced) for the urban energy balance, TARGET and the Urban Weather Generator for the urban heat island, and URock for urban wind fields. The manual is copyright of Fredrik Lindberg, Ting Sun, Sue Grimmond, Yihao Tang and Nils Wallenberg, and the plugin (version 4.6.2 in the repository metadata, QGIS 3 or later) is accessible free from the official QGIS plugin repository and GitHub under GNU GPL v3. Caveats: model outputs depend on the quality of local surface and morphology data, and the manual pages carry 2018 to 2020 copyright while tools keep changing. It supports simulation of heat stress and the cooling effect of green and blue infrastructure in climate adaptation planning; related records are PALM-4U and the Stuttgart green ventilation corridors case study.
